prerequisites: Sufficient knowledge in mathematical-scientific and engineering fundamentals
Advanced knowledge in the respective subject area

learning_outcomes.text: Students know the basic concepts and phases of project management and associated methods and tools.
Students independently delve into a new project-specific task at a scientific level and deepen their knowledge in a special area.
They can organize tasks using project management methods and tools.
Students interpret and question project results regarding their plausibility and classify them with regard to their technical and practical relevance.
Students apply standard and advanced procedures and methods from across their previous studies to solve the task. They use or generate data, evaluate it, and derive solution approaches for the task.
Students adapt project management methods and tools according to the requirements of their project and organize project processing accordingly.
Students develop their own approaches or ideas from various procedures, skills, techniques, and materials to solve the given task.
Students develop and discuss solutions in a group. They convey acquired knowledge and facts to a specialist audience and can discuss and critically question solution concepts with superiors.
Students communicate and present the status of a project in the form of project status reports.

Students develop an awareness of the value of scientific work as the basis for their engineering activities. They justify their professional actions with theoretical and methodical knowledge and take responsibility for the results of their work.

syllabus_topics: Project management: Project initiation (problem analysis, goals)
Project management: Project definition (project organization, procedural models)
Project management: Project planning (structure, process, time, capacities and resources, risks, quality, costs)
Project management: Project implementation with control/monitoring
Project: Analysis of the task and definition of objectives
Project: Planning according to project management
Project: Technical and economic evaluation of selected solutions
assessment_rules: The graded examination performance includes the technical documentation in the form of a written project report (approx. 15 - 30 pages per project group member). The ungraded examination performance consists of a written project report on the project's project management (e.g., with the project structure plan, schedule, and project status report, approx. 12 - 15 pages) and a presentation of the project within the framework of a project fair (approx. 15 minutes).
